name: Acqua Pazza Chicken
allergy: Contains tree nuts.
description: Acqua pazza or crazy water is one of our favourite sauces. Usually served with lightly poached fresh fish, this rich and savory sauce is remarkably simple to make, yet also extremely complex. The use of fresh summer veggies help create a strong flavor base (much like a mirepoix) from which we then layer on the richness of ripe cherry tomatoes and inject a shot of umami from the capers and artichoke hearts. Pair that with some shallow pan-fried chicken thighs and you're gonna want to acqua pazza everything for the next week.

name: Aji Coconut Chicken Stew
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
We love our chilis, but once it a while we taste one that significantly changes our world view on chillis. Meet the Aji Amarillo. We first met this burst of sunshine in our adventures in Peru. We were awed by the vibrant color it had, and floored by how floral and fruity a chili could taste. Spicy? A little…. but oh so much more complex. If you could taste a sunshine, this is what it would taste like.
For this stew we doubled down on the theme of sunshine by adding a healthy dose of summer squashes, a coconut base to both cut the spice and enhance the fruity notes, and a handful of garden peas. One spoonful, and we’ll have you grinning ear to ear even on the most overcast of days

name: Ancho Chicken Fajitas
allergy: May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Is it a taco? No....it's better! We love the way fajitas are traditionally served: sizzling over a hot plate, smothered with caramelized onions and peppers along with freshly toasted tortillas ready to be wrapped. While we can't duplicate the sizzling hot plate, we sure can recreate all the other elements.
PS: Don't skimp on the tangy chipotle salsa. Go ahead, drizzle (or douse) that all over your fajita... a little mess never killed anyone.

name: Anything
allergy: Contains seafood. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Ever asked someone the question "What would you like to eat", only to get the headache-inducing answer of "Anything"? (You have our sympathies.) It's an easy answer, but "anything" is actually a really hard request to fulfill. We bet that you've also learned (hopefully not the hard way) that "anything" is never truly anything.
So here's something to help you out: A dish that could be chicken or pork, meaty yet full of veggies, light tasting yet with enough sauce to down a bowl of rice. Quick to cook, and even quicker to eat, this dish will definitely hit the spot, especially on days when you don't quite know what you want. Now Anything is really possible.
PS: Inspired by the time we ordered "anything" 14 years ago from a little chinese takeout in the middle of rural USA, and was served this amazing dish.

name: Assam Curry Chicken
allergy: Contains soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: We did it! A 10 ingredient fresh curry in under 10 minutes. We start off by grinding and pounding the 10 traditional ingredients (fresh turmeric, galangal, ginger, lime leaves, candlenut, shrimp paste, garlic, chillis, shallots and lemon grass) into a spice paste then seal it in with the chicken to ensure maximum flavor absorption. Pair there with a handful of long beans and a sprig of curry leaves and you'll have a curry that even your grandma would be proud of.

name: Ayam Sambal Cabe Ijo
allergy: May contain traces of tree nuts.
description: Not all sambals have to be scary. Made with mild green chilis and bursting full of aromatics, this green flora sambal has quickly become a staple in our kitchen! Top it on chicken, fish, even air-fried tofu, this sambal will instantly become your new best friend.

name: Banana Leaf Wrapped Ikan Bakar
allergy: Contains seafood, gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: A dish inspired by the idyllic Malaysian beach vacations we used to have as kids. Watching local fisherman grill up freshly caught fish drenched in sambal and kecap manis remains one of our best memories. We may not be able to remember the exact beach or restaurant, but that waft of grilled banana leaf and batang (Spanish mackerel) will forever remain seared into our hearts. For this kit, we made it into an oven kit: if you get it right, you'll be able to get that same gentle fragrance of grilled banana leaf wafting through your home - try it and let us know!

name: Bang Bang Chicken
allergy: Contains tree nuts.
description:
Bang bang traditionally refers to the sticks (Bang 棒) used to smash and shred the chicken into strips. For us though the bang bang evokes memories of those red chained lunar new year firecrackers: each chicken strip, a little fire cracker, popping and bursting with flavor as you chew. Tangy, nutty, crispy, tender every mouthful starts and ends with a bang of pure enjoyment!
PS: We like it warm, but you can also store it in the fridge and serve it as a cold appetizer for those busy lazy-to-cook days

name: Beans & Mince
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
This is the dish we cooked when we had our first lesson in fire control. First off, low heat is used to extract the fragrance from the ginger, garlic dried chillis, shallots, and our secret ingredient, the Szechuan peppercorn (Yes! The ma in mala). Next, the heat is upped to sear the beans and give it a bit of a head start. Lastly, with everything in, the pan goes onto high heat to develop and light crust on the meat and bring our the char and smokiness in the pork without drying it out. Yummm
No eyebrows were burnt when making this dish....that was when we tried to flambe >_<

name: Bittergourd in Black Bean Sauce
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
We tend to use tartness and acid to help balance out the umami notes of a dish, but have you tried using the oft-maligned taste, bitter, instead?
Bitter gourd is one of our favorite ways to do this! The gourd starts off by acting as a sponge, soaking up the deep savory black bean sauce. Its natural bitter-sweet profile (think of a really dark chocolate or mole) then helps to cut through the initial savory-ness of the sauce, while each subsequent bites releases more sauce creating a time-release capsule of umami goodness. Toss in few more textures in the forms of carrots and mince and get ready to discover your new favorite dish.

name: Black Pepper Beef
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Our own rendition of a local zi-char favourite. We've taken extra attention to slice the meat diagonally against the grain to ensure that every piece has enough surface area to soak up the peppery sauce, while remaining tender no matter how you cook it.

name: Bo Luc Lac (Viet-Style Shaking Beef)
allergy: Contains soy, gluten, shellfish (from oyster sauce) May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
A great cut of beef doesn't always have to be eaten as a steak (GASP!). Sure it's an amazing way to enjoy the full flavor of the beef, but try this method and you'll soon find yourself squirreling away a piece of your steak to do a luc lac!
PS: We've been told that the authentic way is to use the filet.... for us, we prefer something a tad more flavorful yet still pretty tender: the striploin. 
PPS: Yes, luc lac means to shake....so shake this bad boy vigorously in the pan while it sears. Just promise to keep those precious cubes in the pan.

name: Braised Cabbage hearts
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Wedge salads are good; but braise it in a tomato base and topped with a tangy tahini pomegranate dressing and it'll become great!

name: Bulbs and Spears
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Looks like an onion....cooks like an onion....but crisps like a snap pea and explodes into a subtle sweet nutty pocket of "what is that i just ate?" 
Liliy Bulbs (Bai He) are not something you see everyday, and tastes nothing like you've had. Pair this with the similarly unique tasting asparagus and meaty shiitakes and you'll have a dish that may change your perceptions of what a vegetarian dish could taste like.

name: Cabbage Chap Chye
allergy: Contains gluten, crustaceans, fish. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: A dish everyone knows and probably orders once a week. That said, nobody actually knows the name of it. We see it at our economic rice stall, our Teochew porridge, sometimes even at our favorite ayam bakar store...it's now just awkward to ask

name: Calabrese Pasta
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: We love a good bomba calabrese sauce.....but as the name sounds, man is it spicy. To make this a lot more friendly, we went to work making our own. The result? A milder calabrese sauce packed with more sweetness and floral notes than usual. Sure, it isn't your traditional bomba calabrese, but load that sauce on top of some pasta primavera and you fool people into thinking you've stood over the stove for hours making this sauce (well we did, so you didn't have to).

name: Carb Free Knife Shaved "Noodles"
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Noodles without the carbs.....too good to be true? Not if you have a peeler, some mushrooms and LOTS of patience. These shaved noodles soak up any amazing sauce you'd want to add; add in a heaping handful of napa cabbage and vegetables and you can say goodbye to instant noodles and hello to a guilt free midnight supper.

name: Caribbean Style Jerk Chicken
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
We love animals, so when it comes to choosing which chickens to eat, we pick the badly behaved ones...the jerks (hehe sorry for the fowl language ). Ok fine, Jerk is a method of cooking that involves marinating meats in an aromatic blend of spices (pimento, cinnamon, nutmeg...etc).
Usually, it also comes with fiery habaneros; for a moment, we considered using the Carolina reaper growing in our backyard, but wisely decided against it. For now, we've kept the spice level down by switching in mild red chillis and adding spring onions to mimic the oomph. That said, if you're feeling up to the challenge, feel free to add in more chillis. You won't regret it.

name: Caribbean Style Jerk Fish
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Definition of a fisherman: A jerk on one end of a line waiting for a jerk on the other end. Ok fine, Jerk is a method of cooking that involves marinating meats in an aromatic blend of spices (pimento, cinnamon, nutmeg...etc).
Usually, it also comes with fiery habaneros; for a moment, we considered using the Carolina reaper growing in our backyard, but wisely decided against it. For now, we've kept the spice level down by switching in mild red chillis and adding spring onions to mimic the oomph. That said, if you're feeling up to the challenge, feel free to add in more chillis. You won't regret it.

name: Cashew Chicken
allergy: Contains soy, gluten, traces of crustaceans and tree nuts
description: You have to be NUTS to not like this combination. The natural sweetness from the peppers, the crunch of the cashews and the umami smokiness of the sauce....mmmm...... there is just NUT-ing better.

name: Cashew Cream Fungi Pasta
allergy: Contains gluten and tree nuts
description: We love a good alfredo sauce....the butter, the cheese, the hint of cream. Pair that with a heap of mushrooms and garden peas and watch us lick that plate clean. Now what if we told you we've made all that dairy-free and vegan! Using our own freshly made cashew cream, we've managed to recreate the creamy texture that'll make you re-think the need to add heavy cream into anything.

name: Cauliflower Shawarma Bake
allergy: May contain traces of nuts
description:
Yes...shawarma is technically a meat dish, but we liked the spices so much that we thought we'd throw in all 10 spices with some cauliflower, the meatiest veggie we know. A handful of chickpeas and sweet potatoes later and bam! Get ready to starfish on the couch and nurse that food baby.
PS did we mention that it also so comes with cheese...mmmm (unless you're vegan, then skip the cheese and say mmmmmm)

name: Cha Ca (Turmeric Dill Seabass)
allergy: Contains seafood. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Turmeric marinated fish pan-seared over high heat with a fistful of aromatic herbs....need we say more? We skipped the shrimp paste to make it a tad more kid friendly but dialed up the dill to really bring home the freshness and natural sweetness of the seabass.
We like this dish so much we're contemplating adding dill to our planter boxes...

name: Chayote Stir-fry
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Sometimes known as "Buddha's Palm", this gourd is great with stir-fried over high heat with your favorite vegetables. While it tastes not so great raw, a bit of heat and a few key supporting side veggies will help bring out its natural sweetness while retaining the lovely crunch synonymous with a summer squash salad.

name: Chipotle Peri Peri Chicken and Veggies
allergy: Contains soy, gluten and traces of tree nuts
description: This is not the usual peri-peri that you're used to, but be careful, cos this packs a punch! We've added adobo chilis and smoked paprika to bring out a natural sweet smokiness to the sauce. So sit back, watch it grill in your oven, and get ready for some fireworks.

name: Chop Chop Red Braised Chicken
allergy: Contains traces of gluten and tree nuts
description:
Hong Shao or red braising is a technique that we've been obsessed with since childhood. Usually done with pork belly, the art of slow braising shaoxing, sugar and soy sauce results in probably the most succulent and savory sauce one can think of.
Keeping in mind our time crunched schedules and our ever expanding waistlines, we've opted to red braise chicken along with hearty mix of bamboo shoots and shiitake mushrooms for this recipe. Along with a bowl of perfectly steamed short grain rice, this recipe is bound to having everyone asking for seconds! Ok maybe it won't be that good for our waistlines after all.

name: Citrus Braised Salmon (Serves 2)
allergy: Contains fish, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
We love a good old fashioned to end the day, but what do you do with all that leftover orange?
You braise a fish of course. OK, maybe that's not the most natural next step (that would be to just have more drinks), but hey, we did and we can't get enough of it. The citrus helps cut the fattiness of that hunk of salmon, while also slowly pickling the red-onions as it stews in all those juices at the bottom. At the top, the orange and lemon peels start to crisp, creating mini pockets of crunch.

name: Coconut Curry Chicken
allergy: Contains seafood, tree nuts.
description: KFC uses 11 spices and herbs? So do we! First we marinated the chicken with an 11-ingredient rempah (spice paste) that we make in-house from scratch. All you have to do is add in the coconut milk and into the oven a for an easy, tasty, freshly made meal. Rice optional!

quantity.raw: Mild Red Chilis, Garlic, Shallots, Candlenut, Fresh Turmeric, Galangal, Belacan, Lemongrass, Lime Leaves, Sugar, Salt

name: Coconut Curry Salmon
allergy: Contains seafood and tree nuts.
description: This is salmon with an Asian twist. We first layer in an 11-ingredient rempah (spice paste) that we make in-house from scratch, and then add coconut milk to the mix. Pop into the oven and let the salmon stew in all that goodness for an easy, tasty, freshly made meal. Rice optional!

quantity.raw: Mild Red Chilis, Garlic, Shallots, Candlenut, Fresh Turmeric, Galangal, Belacan, Lemongrass, Lime Leaves, Sugar, Salt

name: Coffee Pork Collar
allergy: Contains crustaceans, soy, gluten and traces of tree nuts.
description: A staple in our weekly zi char dinners, this sweet, tangy with a hint of bitter from the coffee glaze goes well on almost anything. While traditionally slathered on deep-fried bone in ribs, we’ve opted for the more home kitchen friendly pork collar cubes. More surface area means more nooks and crannies for the sauce to cover!

name: Crisp Greens in Silky Sauce
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
A blast from the past! We've all had a variation of this dish sometime in our childhood...especially when the adults were feeling hardworking and inspired to cook. With 6 different vegetables to prep, it's no wonder this dish went extinct faster than we can say "seconds!"
Thankfully now you have us to do all the slicing, peeling, and de-bearding (yes all the things we have to do for this dish)....Enjoy!

name: Crispy Salt and Pepper Pork
allergy: May contain traces of tree nuts
description: This is the dish we had to cook 3 times before we even got a single picture, because we just couldn’t stop picking at it. It could be the addictiveness of the Szechuan peppercorns, or the mix of marbled pork collar and fresh herbs...either way, this is one that will leave you wanting more.

name: Dairy-free "Butter" Chicken
allergy: Contains tree nuts
description:
Our go-to dish when we crave a curry, it goes well with naan, rice, prata, even chips (man do we miss those pub days)! Alas sometimes our body doesn't agree with all that butter and dairy. Thankfully we've found a slight work-around, one that uses freshly ground cashew butter as a substitute
PS: We've kept this curry slightly chunkier than the traditional, letting the tomatoes, onions and herbs really shine. Another twist: stirring in some wilted spinach not only gives it a color pop, but also makes it a nicely balanced meal

name: Dak-Galbi (Spicy Chicken)
allergy: Contains gluten, crustaceans, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: When we used to live in Seoul, every year, during the coldest month of the year, we'd venture 3 hours out of the city to a little place called Hwacheon to go ice-fishing. On our way back, we'd be sure to stop by Chuncheon for their famous ddakgalbi. Juicy chicken thighs, perilla leaves, rice cakes, cabbage.....all smothered in a rich red pepper-based sauce, yum. Did we mention that it is all cooked and crisped in a humongous cast iron pan? Yes....YUM. Even though we can't go this year, we can still try to re-invent the magic by making it into a kit! Now...if only we can also re-create the fried rice that comes after.

name: Dry Pot Cauliflower
allergy: Contains gluten, crustaceans, fish. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: There is a surprising amount of liquid that goes in this dish, but it gets its name from the technique of letting the vegetables absorb all that sauce and juices till the pot is dry, the sauce thickens, and the veggies start to char a bit around the edges. The result, an intense burst of flavor with every bite.

name: Easy Peasy Bok Choi
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Need to eat more veggies, but also kinda over raw salads? Well, we have a quick 4-minute dish for you. Separating the juicy stems from the tender leaves, allows you to cook them both to perfection. Sprinkle on some goji berries and mushrooms and no one is going to believe that you only spent 4 minutes on this.

name: Firecracker Beef
allergy: Contains gluten and traces of tree nuts.
description: Our go-to carb topper. Be it noodles, rice or even a toasted butter brioche, this topper is going to make it taste AH-mazing!  Savory mince seasoned with a sweet and tangy honey sriracha sauce, then smothered with shredded brussel sprouts....need we say more?

name: Galilee Cod Skewers
allergy: Contains seafood. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description: Made with plump Atlantic cod all marinated in a bright sunny marinade of spices, herbs and lemons, this BBQ staple is a delicious reminder of those seaside BBQs awesome weekends are made of. Yes...it may be a school day, but bring on the beach vibes (but please no sand)!

name: Ginger Miso Salmon
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Probably our most versatile kit yet: Pan fry it or pop it into the oven...up to you!
Pan-frying gives the salmon a nice crust and reduces the ginger miso sauce to a glaze-like consistency, coating every bite with a punch of umami.
Oven baking lets the water from the veggies mix with the sauce bringing out the lighter more floral ginger notes. Also....no mess!

name: Ginger Scallion Fish
allergy: Contains fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
One of our favorite dishes of all time is the Cantonese style ginger scallion steamed fish ( it's probably why we show up to weddings...sorry friends). That said we're also extremely lazy and having to bust out the steamer AND a pan is sometimes just too much trouble. Enter our preferred home rendition of the traditional dish.
Made into a stir-fry, we've also added in both scallions and spring onions to layer in the texture and sweetness while also reducing the bite from the ginger. Top it off with the nuttiness of the shimeji mushrooms get ready to ask for a second bowl of rice.

name: Gochujang mackerel
allergy: Contains gluten and traces of tree nuts.
description:
We love a grilled fish, especially one that's been slathered and coated with a sweet chili marinade! You've tasted our rendition of the local Ikan Bakar, now we'll take you north to the beaches of Korea for our other favorite style.
The savory notes of the slightly fermented Korean pepper paste helps to bring out the natural sweetness of the mackerel while the Napa cabbage salad helps to keep your palate cleansed so that every bite is as good as your first!

name: Golden Caramel Braised Chicken
allergy: Contains seafood, gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Hamburgers in the US, ramen in Japan, what do you get when you want fast-food in China? Well this of course. Traditionally served bubbling in an earthenware clay pot filled with toppings of your choice, this belly warming meal is best served with a generous bowl of rice or 2. Just make sure you put aside some time to nurse the inevitable food coma. YUM

name: Hawaiian Hoisin Pork
allergy: Contains seafood, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Pork has always been a great meat to use when pairing with marinades, but this combination becomes life altering when pineapples come into the picture. The bromelain in pineapples are great at breaking down muscle fiber, yielding meat that is not just tender but also full of that yummy marinade. What marinade you ask? Well we can only think of one that goes well with the tartness of pineapples.... a Hawaiian inspired hoisin base.
YUM

name: Home-style chicken and cordyceps
allergy: Contains traces of gluten and tree nuts
description: One benefit of living in Singapore is being in the middle of a culinary melting pot where amazing food is just a stones throw from your doorstep. That said, if you're anything like us, you often find yourself craving something homey, simple but still bursting with flavor. When we get that feeling, we default to this dish, where the ingredients do the talking: Sweetness from the wongbok, umami from the shiitakes, earthiness from the cordyceps and fragrance from the garlic/ginger/scallion medley. A light coating of a miso based sauce and homey never tasted this good.

name: Honey Ginger Chicken
allergy: Contains soy, gluten, crustacean products, fish products, tree nuts
description: Simple is sometimes better, especially when the ingredients are good. Honey instead of sugary syrups means you get a more complex floral flavor while the use of young grated ginger cuts the richness without the spicy kick.

name: Honey Ginger Pork Belly
allergy: Contains soy, gluten, crustacean products, fish products, tree nuts
description: Simple is sometimes better, especially when the ingredients are good. Honey instead of sugary syrups means you get a more complex floral flavor while the use of young grated ginger cuts the richness without the spicy kick.

name: Honey Mustard Glazed Salmon
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Tangy dijon mustard, sweet smoked paprika, real honey (not syrup). Now that's how you make a real good glaze. Pair that with a nice slab of salmon and you've got yourself an amazing dinner with almost no prep time or clean-up. The hardest part: waiting for the fish to come out of the oven.

name: Jamaican Kabocha Soup
allergy: May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Yes the ABC soup is a good easy soup, but sometimes we want something a tad more tropical. Inspired by the simplicity of the ABC, we swapped out the traditional ABC veggies for some of our favorites:

Kabocha (Japanese pumpkin): Adds delicate sweet chestnut note while keeping the heft you get from potatoes
Chayote: Soaks up the flavor of the broth while maintaining its texture. a great way to lift and soften the overwhelming sweetness from stewed carrots
Carrots/Corn: Why mess with a great formula

Add in a splash of coconut water, and this tropical soup will be your next best diet friend

name: Japanese Style Beef Fried Rice
allergy: Contains crustaceans, gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Beef Fried Rice.....nuff said.
One of our all time favorite things to do after a BBQ: gather up all the meat drippings and scraps, add a bit of our special sauce, maybe a bit of vegetables, and then RICE. Let that rice soak up all the goodness as it chars in  all that naturally flavored oil and juices. Sometime, we think that's actually the best part of the meal.

name: Kale + Chicken Lemak
allergy: Contains seafood, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: We love a good lemak. What is that? It's a way of cooking that leverages the sweetness and creaminess of coconut milk to extract the full flavor of the ingredients. A good base is key and we make ours with a freshly grounded mix of 11 herbs and spices. Toss in some kale to really soak up all that coco-nutty goodness, and a dash of ginger flower to brighten up the stew an you get a light curry that is both rich, creamy but also easy on the palette.

name: Kansai Style Gyudon
allergy: Contains soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Sukiyaki is one of those things we crave every now and then. More often than not, those times tend to coincide with days where we would just like to starfish on the couch and not move. When that happens, we reach for our tried and tested gyudon recipe! The sukiyaki style sauce base creates a warm "under the blanket" feeling, while the gyudon format means we only have 1 bowl to clean….perfect!  We've also added scallions and mushrooms to the traditional onion base to add an additonal subtle layer of flavor while cutting the fattiness of the beef.

PS: Crack and egg over it in the last 30 seconds of cooking and you'll bring this dish to another level!

name: Kecap Manis Beef
allergy: Contains soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Slices of tender cross-cut beef flank generously coated with spicy kecap manis sauce can't get any better can it? Oh yes it can, especially when it is layered on top of an anti jelak-ifying lemongrass and ginger base. Now that's a dish we can eat everyday.

name: Kimchi Pork Belly
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy. May contain traces of gluten and tree nuts
description:
Ever put something at the back of your fridge only to forget about it? We do that all the time! Thankfully, when it comes to kimchi, it means it we get to enjoy one of our all time favourites: stir-fried kimchi. We age our kimchi till it gets to a PH level of 4.2; the perfect sweetness and twang for making stews and stir-frys.
PS: We forgot to mention the heaping serving of pork belly.....this dish is our favourite for a reason.

name: Kimchi Stew
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy. May contain traces of gluten and tree nuts
description: This humble dish has been credited with everything from curing a raging hangover to single handedly keeping the SARS virus away from South Korea. We don't know if any of it is true but man, is it delicious. Decadent pork belly balanced with the tartness of perfectly ripened kimchi....a great way to kick start "you" time after a long day at work.

name: Kinpira Burdock and Carrots
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
You'll often see this as a side dish in your favorite bento or Japanese meal....if you're anything like us, you've probably routinely lament about the small serving size and possibly even shamelessly ask for more. 
Kinpira is a method of first sautéing, then simmering in a stock; one that works amazingly well with crunchy vegetables. The sautéing helps to soften the vegetables allowing them to fully absorb all that yummy stock used in the simmering process. While a little patience is required, following these steps will yield a scrumptious side dish that can be consumed both warm or cold.... perfect for batch cooking!

name: Korean Miso Braise
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
One of the 3 great sauces of Korean cuisine, doenjang, or Korean miso as we like to call it, it a pantry staple for most Korean families. While it is most commonly found in stews, our favorite way of consuming this is in the form of a thick gravy (think the sauce that tops a hor-fun or mui-fan).
Slightly edgier than its Japanese counterpart, this miso first allows the natural sweetness of the onions to shine, then the soy notes show up enhancing the firm tofu in the dish, lastly the fermented notes (the ones that make this sauce so special) kicks in and helps to elevate the pork belly while cutting the fat found in such a savory cut. Serve this over rice or plain white noodles and get ready to ask for seconds!

name: Kung Pao Beef
allergy: Contains soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Isn't this usually with chicken? Yes it is, but we found out that pairing the same amazing sauce with our cross cut beef flank not only makes the sauce fully seep into and marinate every slice of meat, the dish also cooks in half the time. Talk about fast food.

quantity.raw: Water, Cornstarch, Sugar, Shaoxing wine, Rice vinegar, Light soy sauce, Dark soy sauce, Salt

name: Kung Pao Chicken
allergy: Contains soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Comfort food at its finest. This dish was so loved by the public that they even re-named it hu-la chicken (糊辣鸡丁) to avoid association with the imperial regime during the chinese cultural revolution. Anything to continue eating this highly addictive dish.

quantity.raw: Water, Cornstarch, Sugar, Shaoxing wine, Rice vinegar, Light soy sauce, Dark soy sauce, Salt

name: LA Galbi
allergy: Contains gluten and traces of tree nuts.
description:
People are often surprised to find out that our favorite cut of beef is the short rib. Not only is it well marbled, it is also packed with flavor rarely found in the more premium sections. Braised, stewed, pressure cooked, on an asador, you name it, we love it.
One of our all-time favorite ways to enjoy short rib though, is the LA galbi. Firstly, the short-rib is sliced flank wise across the bone, yielding strips of tender meat great for marinating. Sealing it in with our freshly made marinade of crushed pears, onions and soy and there you have it - the ultimate stove top grilling dish. 
Of course, no Korean style BBQ is complete without healthy heap of lightly dressed salad to pair with that amazing dish you just made.

name: Ladolemono Pan-seared Fish
allergy: Contains seafood. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description: Plump Atlantic cod, seared to perfection delicately flavored with a bright lemon dill sauce. Served with juicy tomatoes and fluffy cous cous. A refreshing and flavorful dish for any occasion.

name: Lebanese Tacos (Lahm Bil Ajeen)
allergy: Contains gluten and traces of tree nuts.
description:
How do we feed ourselves in the Prepped household? Well...with this hack of a recipe! The perfect quick snack, this middle eastern delight is a great way to have a meal ready in a few minutes that you can eat on the go!
Traditionally served on flatbread, we instead chose to slather our amazing meat mixture on a tortilla (both to reduce the cooking time, but also because our waistlines were getting a bit too big from eating all that dough). For you guys, we added a salad topper to add a bit of razzle dazzle and make it a complete meal.

name: Lemon Butter Seabass
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Sometimes the simplest ingredients can create the most luxurious sauces. Here, the butter is key! At the start, cilantro and garlic is used to infuse the sauce with a touch of lightness and kick. As the butter browns, it starts to release the trademark nuttiness which is also when you'd want to remove it from the stove and set to cool. Add a touch of lemon juice and salt, and get ready to elevate any dish with the richest 3 ingredient sauce you'll ever make.

name: Lemon Chicken Piccata
allergy: May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
A tad more complicated than our usual one pot recipes, but a ton more rewarding! Crispy chicken medallions smothered by a tangy mushroom caper sauce, what's not to love? Great on its own or topped over a bed of pasta with a glass of white wine, get ready to make every night a date night.....even if it is just yourself and your TV (clearly this happens to us a lot).
PSSSST: We're gonna let you in on a little secret to guarantee your chicken turns out crispy - dredge it with corn starch instead of flour (it's included!)

name: Lemongrass Chicken with Cellophane noodles
allergy: Contains seafood, gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
A saucier version of a traditional thai style grilled chicken (Gai Yang), literally.  While this dish usually comes with a tamarind based dipping sauce, we've opted instead to keep all those flavors in the marinade so your chicken gets the maximum amount of flavor absorption.
Unsure about tamarind? Not to worry, we've kept that element separate as a side sauce. Use it to dip the chicken or pour it over your cellophane noodles for an irresistable side dish...your choice!

name: Malai Chicken Tikka
allergy: Contains gluten and tree nuts.
description:
Juicy chicken medallions rubbed with a 10 ingredient spice blend THEN marinated in a cashew yoghurt cream base.....need we keep going? You know this is going to be good. Grill it, bake it, air-fry it.... it really doesn’t matter how you decide to cook it, this is going to come out fabulous.
Oh and don't forget the shredded coconut cucumber salad tossed with herbs and crushed peanuts.
Probably our most awesome kit yet!

name: Maple Plum Coated Brussels Sprouts
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
What's tender on the inside, crispy on the outside and coated with a savory sweet plum glaze? The perfect brussels sprout of course. Toss in some chili oil and you'll be wondering why you didn't eat brussels sprouts sooner.
PS: See if you can taste a hint of our secret ingredient (if you need a clue....look at the ingredients on the label)

name: Mapo Tofu
allergy: Contains soybeans, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
I always thought Ma (麻) stood for hot and if i wanted to grow up into a Mapo (麻婆: hot older lady) i should eat more of this, afterall you are what you eat right? Alas Mapo 麻婆 really meant pock-faced lady....if only i can stop eating this.
PS: We've provided extra peppercorns for those who enjoy an extra jolt of numbness

name: Married Me Chicken
allergy: Contains traces of gluten and tree nuts
description:
Marry me chicken was a staple during our dating years, a dish that is easy to make, difficult to screw up  and impressive to anyone you are making it for.
Now that we're married and have gotten even lazier, we've started cooking the carb (orzo) directly in the same pan so that we have one less thing to clean.  Just as hearty as when we first had it, but now with a lot less pretense and a whole lot more enjoyment. I guess that's what married life is huh.

name: Midnight Tonjiru
allergy: Allergy information: Contains seafood and traces of tree nuts
description:
Inspired by one of our favorite Netflix shows to binge on! (we watched the intro so much that we had to try and recreate the dish)
Things you'd love about this dish:

Making your own kombu dashi from scratch (using our little tea bags)
Feeling grounded and so close to nature from the earthiness of burdock
The mix of textures between the give of the daikon, the bounciness of the konnyaku and the crunch of the root vegetables
The warmth from the rich savory taste of red miso

Share it with a friend, or do what we do and savor it slowly on your next Netflix binge marathon!

name: Miso Glazed Vegetables
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Grilling veggies are always an easy way to make a good quick healthy meal. But before you tuck in, how about take another 5 more minutes to glaze it with 2 types of miso before broiling it again. You’ll be rewarded for your patience with what is most probably the best vegetarian/vegan friendly dish you’ll ever have. Don’t say we didn’t warn you: you may actually forget that you were once an omnivore.

name: Miyeokguk (Korean Seaweed Soup)
allergy: Contains seafood, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Chicken soup for the soul? We prefer miyeok-guk aka Korean seaweed soup. Traditionally eaten on birthdays, we also like to have it on weekdays, holidays, sick days....well....basically any day. 
Sautéing the beef in fragrant sesame oil creates the first layer of this rich and meaty broth. Next the seaweed and dried oysters impart a silky texture to the soup, adding hints of smoke and sea to the broth. Let this simmer for as long as you can control yourself and you'd be rewarded with a soupy stew that's both rich in nutrients and low in calories.
PS: Jazz it up with shredded omelets, tofu, or rice cakes. not strictly traditional, but very good nonetheless

name: Mojo Chicken with Texas Caviar
allergy: Contains tree nuts.
description: A Cuban inspired dish, this tangy citrus based marinade, chock full of spices and herbs, is one of our best kept secrets when we need to tenderize some chicken. Pair that with a warm cous cous black bean salad (also known as cowboy caviar) and you'll feel ready to bust out that ol' mojo and to party into the sunset! Yeehaw!

name: Moo Shu Pork
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
No no...not the fan favorite from our childhood Disney Mulan, but a fan favorite none the less. While it is traditionally eaten wrapped in delicate Chinese pancakes, we like ours hearty, either on a bowl of rice or on some somen noodles along with an extra handful of shiitake mushrooms and red cabbage.
Regardless of your carb choice, this gravylicious dish will be a welcome addition to your weekday repertoire.

name: Nam Tok (Waterfall Steak Salad)
allergy: Contains seafood and traces of tree nuts
description:
The waterfall like sizzle, crackle, pop sound that this succulently marinated steak makes when it hits a hot grill/pan is what gives it its namesake. I know..... i know, we too have never heard a waterfall sizzle but hey....who are we to argue?
Regardless of whether it sizzles, crackles or pops, the tender juicy steak pieces paired with a crisp herb salad tossed with our secret smokey dressing is bound to send of waves flavors cascading  and crashing into your taste buds,....just like a waterfall!

name: Negima Yakitori Skewers
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Chicken and leek skewers have always been our go to yakitori flavor, a simple combination that is equal parts savory and healthy (that's what we tell ourselves...after all, it has vegetables in it and is most definitely healthier than the pure chicken skin skewer).  While some love it with just salt and pepper, we like ours drenched in tare (sauce); not just any tare, but the one traditionally used for grilled eels. Not the most traditional, but just the way we like it.
PS: Line the bottom of the tray with rice and let it soak up all the tare and juices as you baste and grill those skewers to perfection

name: No Fry Gobi Manchurian
allergy: May contain traces of nuts
description:
One of our all time favorite indian-chinese dishes! Breaded cauliflower perfectly deep fried and tossed in a sweet garlicy chili sauce....what's not to like? The cooking process of course! 
Thankfully we've discovered a method that avoids deep-frying altogether. Sure it requires a bit of a workaround, and the availability of an oven/air fryer, but once you have that settled we've got everything else covered...down to that awesome garlicky sweet chili sauce.

name: Old cucumber chicken soup
allergy: May contain traces of tree nuts.
description: Young is not always better, leave a cucumber on the vine to ripen/mature and you get a brown firm vegetable perfectly concentrated with flavor. While it may not taste crisp and cooling like a green cucumber, the old cucumber is actually known as the perfect ingredient to create cooling "Yin" soups to counteract the sweltering heat of our little island.

name: One Pan Japchae
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
The best thing about mum coming over to visit is all the food she leaves in our fridges. Our favourite has always been her japchae. It's a dish full of love as every element has to be individually cooked, then mixed in at the end. Now that we're *ahem* adults (we think), no one leaves us food anymore T.T .
If you find yourself in the same boat, fret not, here is a kit for japchae, and the best thing is: we've condensed it so you can whip it all up in one pan!

name: Ooey Gooey Marmite Steak
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: This may get a bit divisive... but trust us: a bit of honey and a dash of Worcestershire will transform this into the ultimate umami bomb. Add in a medley of peppers and some tender flank steak and your belly can thank us while you concentrate on fighting that post meal food coma.

name: Pan Seared Georgian Beef
allergy: Contains soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Traditionally cooked over a grill in the form of a kebab, we've decided to make it a bit more friendly to our highly dense living format by removing the skewer! 
We marinate chunky cubes of NZ striploin with a blend of 6 spices, enhancing the rich deep taste of grass-fed beef. Layer on a cucumber dill relish to cut the richness of the beef and get ready for a summer dish for your next pool party! 
Best part: it takes all of 10 minutes to whip up a dish to impress.

name: Pandan Chicken Rice
allergy: Contains crustaceans, gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
We love pandan chicken, but we're also too lazy to individually wrap each chicken piece. Our solution? The lasagna method!
First, freshly made pandan extract is infused into the marinade. Next, we sandwich the rice with 2 layers of pandan leaves, ensuring that the pandan aroma gets infused into the rice. On top of that we layer on the marinated chicken and yet another layer of pandan. As the chicken cooks, the juices and drippings will start percolating downwards, adsorbing even more pandan flavor as they channel its way through the grains of rice, creating pockets of flavor waiting for you to discover.
Best thing? It can all be done in an oven!

name: Potsticker tacos
allergy: Contains traces of gluten and tree nuts
description:
Potsticker dumplings are amazing when freshly mixed, and wrapped potstickers are even better....that is if you are actually good at wrapping them. Alas our fat fingers and lack of dexterity makes the pursuit of potsticker happiness a futile one. So what did we do?
Well, we turned our potstickers into an open faced taco-esque frisbee of awesomeness. Juicy meat on a thin crispy shell, topped with a tangy cabbage slaw, all made in under 10 minutes. What's not to like?

name: Qinglong Medley
allergy: Contains soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Qinglong is the kobe beef equivalent of vegetables: The spicy garlic-ky top half is chopped off to use as fertilizer while exposure to sunlight is strictly controlled throughout the different stages of growth. This results in a tender and mild tasting chive, the perfect companion to a medley of beansprouts and oyster mushrooms.

name: Quesadilla Al Pastor
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Yes, it is traditionally spit roasted and served in a taco…..but there is something about the quesadilla form factor that is just alluring. Maybe it is the melted cheese binding everything together, or the slightly charred crispness of the tortillas. Either way this is sure to be a hit!
Marinated with 3 types of mild ground chilis (Guajillo, Ancho, Paprika), sear this chicken/pork over a hot cast iron pan along with a dash of pineapples for a wonderfully smokey, sweet, lip-puckering meat filling. Now top it up with some cheese, onions and cilantro and choose to eat it as a taco, or a quesadilla!

name: Quick Braised Bulgogi
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: The quintessential Korean experience. We've marinated the beef in our special concoction of soy and apple sauce so all you need to do is throw it in a pan and let it stew in its own juices. Enjoy!

name: Ratatouille Chicken
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Fresh summer vegetables, crispy chicken medallions, and a tangy tomato based sauce; this recipe is great on a bed of pasta or rice and will have you licking your plate clean.
PS: Add a bit more water if you prefer a chunky stew.

name: Red Pepper Chutney Salmon
allergy: Contains seafood. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description: What do you get when you mix freshly roasted peppers and red onions, a tangy honey lime dressing, and a few lugs of  top shelf spanish olive oil? A relish that goes well with almost everything. Our favourite use....to grill fish of course. Thick enough to keep the fish moist, while subtle enough to let the flavor of the fish shine through. One taste and you'd wish we sold this by the jar

quantity.raw: Roasted Red Peppers, Roasted Onions, Honey, Olive Oil, Cilantro, Lemon Juice, Smoked Paprika,

name: Roasted Red Pepper Soup
allergy: Contains gluten May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Creamy soups don't have to be complex or require a ton of cream. All you need is a great tasting vegetable, a blender, and a little bit of patience with the oven. Red peppers are one of our favourite veggies for this, and slow roasting them ensures that the natural sugars have time to develop while excess liquid is removed resulting in a concentrated burst of flavor (think dry aging, but for vegetables).
Pop all these in a blender with a bit of water/stock and be impressed by the gourmet quality soup you've just made.
P.S. Get a hunk of good bread on standby!

name: Sesame Chicken
allergy: Contains traces of gluten and tree nuts
description: No no no, not the deep fried kind you see at your take-out or panda express. We're talking about the real authentic sesame chicken: gently braised with ginger infused aromatic sesame oil, superior soy sauce and a dash of shaoxing wine. This dish is so fragrant, yummy and nutritious that it is traditionally used to nurse new mum's back to health after child birth! Hmm...i wonder if my food baby counts?

name: Smokey Cauliflower Fried Rice
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
A little shout out to our keto and low carb friends!
We tried to recreate a bit of wok-hei by mixing in a touch of liquid smoke into our sauce. Just make sure to sear it on high heat at the end to release all the hickory aromas.
Man do we miss the days we could hot smoke our cauliflower outdoors on an bbq.

name: Smothered Steamed Broccoli
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Smothered, Covered and Capped (if you know, you know) ...except now that we're adults we've created a healthy yet still appetizing version. In place of griddled hash we now have lightly steamed broccoli covered with 3 types of shrooms and smothered with our goji berries/ red date infused sauce. Now that's a guilt-free late-night dinner
PS: if you really want to impress, add a drop of truffle oil and watch this dish transform into one worthy of a banquet dinner

name: Spicy Pork Bulgogi
allergy: Contains soy, traces of seafood, gluten. May also contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
In Korea every restaurant, bar, and hole-in-the-wall drinking establishment has their own rendition of this dish. Every one of them tastes amazing (even our neighborhood grilled mackerel shop made a mean rendition of this dish).
Our rendition is an ode to our favorite version, the aforementioned grilled mackerel shop: Marbled pork collar slices slathered in a spicy garlic-ky marinade sweetened with crushed Naju pears…YASSS. Throw in a handful of shredded veggies and let the wok do the job!
PS: Make it fancy by pairing it with fresh lettuce or perilla leaves to form the ultimate wrap

name: Steamed Kabocha Chicken
allergy: Contains soy, gluten, crustacean products, fish products, tree nuts
description: We usually roast, bake or boil our pumpkins (even carve it sometimes), but steaming it may just be the most underrated method of cooking it. Steaming keeps the flesh nice and delicate while letting the sweetness intensify under the gentle heat of the steam. Pair it with the crisp-ness of chayote and a rock star sauce and "diet food" has never tasted better

name: Steamed Wine Chicken
allergy: Contains soy, gluten, crustacean products, fish products, tree nuts
description: Drunk food is the best, especially when it is the food that's drunk and not you. One of our easiest packs, this dish contrasts the savory-ness of chicken thighs and Shaoxing wine with the healthy influences of ginger, red dates and wolfberries. A taste that you're sure to like, beer goggles or not.

name: Stuffed Gourds and Shrooms
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Now this is how you layer taste profiles: At first bite, the savory meat patties burst with umami, releasing those marinated juices you've spent the last 18 minutes slowly steaming. Then the crunch and sweetness of the water chestnuts kick in as you slowly chew on the rest of the dish. Before you can say "ooo that's too rich" the slight bitterness of the gourd envelopes your taste buds, acting as a palette cleanser, readying you for your next mouthful. Best of all: because this a steamed dish, it isn't such a guilty pleasure that you can't have two more, or three!

name: Sugarcane Chicken Satay
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Not your usual satay skewers! These Thai inspired bad boys lean more to the fragrant tangy side, bursting with floral scents from the ginger flower. To kick it up a notch, all this yumminess is wrapped around a "skewer" made from sugarcane. Be sure to bite down hard and allow the natural sweetness of the sugarcane to further enhance the flavor of your new favorite type of satay.
PS: If you're a straw biter like us, you'll love biting into these sticks of juicy sugarcane...just be careful, they could be a little hot.

name: Taiwanese 3-cup chicken
allergy: Contains soy, gluten May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
All good things comes in threes, even sauces. This mix of shaoxing, sesame oil and soy sauce can make almost anything you throw in there taste good.
*Hint: Don't skimp on the sesame oil.

name: Tangy Larb with Winged Beans
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
We Larb this dish. 
Where should we start? It tastes healthy like a salad, yet still packs a punch with the meat. It's familiar enough, but also has an uncommon vegetable (winged beans) that you can impress your friends and family with. It tastes great right off the hob, but even better the day after straight from the fridge....
Love at first sight? More like Larb at first bite....

name: Thai Chilli Lime Seabass
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Craving something light, healthy and packed full with flavor? We've got just the thing for you: Steamed Fish. Before you dismiss us, just know that the lime will make your lips pucker and the chillis are bound to make your heart skip a beat. Take that for a boring steamed fish.
PS: Be gentle on the chillis

quantity.raw: Fish Sauce, Lime Juice, Water, Sugar

name: Thai Kai Lan with Ginger Flower
allergy: Contains gluten, crustaceans, fish. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Tired of the same old garlic sauteed vegetables? Try this thai inspired rendition instead. Thai brussel sprouts(baby kailan) is a forgiving vegetable suitable for even the greenest of us.
PS: That floral aroma you're tasting for the first time is ginger flower. Yes we had to fight our local rojak seller for it, they are a territorial bunch #hawkertriads

name: Thai Style Pork Collar
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
A super easy kit that will satisfy the carnivore in you (or your life). The savoriness of the marbled pork collar is contrasted perfectly with the tanginess of the lime based fish sauce.
Best thing: everything is chopped so the sauce is a breeze to make.

name: Three Shroom Braise
allergy: Contains Soy, gluten, may contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Why did the wong bok go to the party? Because the party was full of fungi-s (fun guys)  get it?. Ok our humor is pretty bad but hopefully not this dish.
We've created this dish using 3 of our favorite mushrooms:
The buna shimeji adds a nutty crunch, the king oyster has an almost silky abalone texture and taste, while the shiitake is scored so that it soaks up all the sauces and transforms into a juicy pouch bursting with flavor. All these great things, on a bed of sweet braised wong bok.

name: Tom Yum Chicken Fried Rice
allergy: Contains crustaceans, gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
We’re all familiar with the soup, but what if we took all the yummy goodness, condensed it into a paste, and fried some rice with it?
The answer is right here: an uplifting tangy bowl of friend rice bursting with aromatics and flavor. Add in a generous fistful of chicken and a smattering of kalian stems for the crunch and say hello to another fried rice to add to your arsenal of quick lunches

name: Tuscan Salmon
allergy: May contain seafood and tree nuts.
description: As we approach winter (for us, the rainy season) nothing brightens up our day like a recipe straight out of the Tuscan sunshine. Sundried tomatoes, artichoke hearts and ripe olives create a burst of sun scorched flavor. Layer in our favorite summer vegetables and a flakey piece of salmon and a sun filled fun day is never too far away

name: Viet-Cajun Fish with Zoodles
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Cajun....what's that? The short answer is it's a cuisine hailing from southern Louisiana, where the food is steeped in French, Spanish and West African influences. What does it really mean: Great tasting spices. We paired all those spices with the savory-ness of Vietnamese fish sauce and garlic and it immediately brings back memories of those backyard crawfish boils in April. A twirl of zoodles (zucchini) helps to cleanse your pallet so you can dig in for another mouthful.....mmm
PS: If you're afraid of splattering oil, pop everything in the oven with some oil and bake it for 18 minutes. 
PPS: If you're brave, you can cook it for longer; the spices will form a dark crust which also happens to be our preferred way of cooking (blackened fish)....however, it does cause quite a bit of smoke so be warned.

name: Vietnamese Beef Bowl
allergy: Contains seafood and traces of tree nuts
description: Is it a warm salad? Or maybe a noodle dish? We don't really know either, what we do know is that has become a bit of lunch favorite for us. Inspired by the bun pho xao, we kept the noodles constant, but opted to spruce things up with a citrus-fish sauce marinated steak instead of the usual stir-fried strips. Add in a handful of herbs and lunch will become a daily highlight for you too!

name: Vietnamese braised fish (Ca Kho To)
allergy: Contains seafood. May contain traces of tree nuts.
description:
Yes, we may not have a clay pot at home, but that doesn't stop us from making this amazing caramelized braised fish a staple in our weekly rotation. Thick juicy pieces of fish glistening in a glorious coconut water, fish sauce and caramel braise; top this over rice with a side of bok choi and you'll be glad you went home for dinner.
This dish is easy, fuss free yet packed with flavor...the perfect end to a busy day.

name: Warm Summer Sunshine Salad
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Bask in the warmth of our easiest one-pan roasted summer salad. This refreshing mix of slow roasted sweet potatoes, hand shucked fresh corn, and snaps of asparagus all tossed in a snazzy preserved lemon caper dressing is bound to make the rainy days disappear.
PS: Did we mention that it's a one pan recipe!

name: Whatever (Ginger scallion chicken)
allergy: May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Whatever? What is a whatever? How does one eat a whatever? So what do you do when the answer you get, to the perfectly normal question of "what would you like to eat", is a very futile and enigmatic "whatever"?
Well, from the team that gave you Anything, we present Whatever: Healthy-ish marinated steamed chicken pieces topped with a colorful, packed full of flavor ginger scallion sauce. Garnish with a few carrots and you have a dish that will appeal to even the most uninterested eater.

name: Wine Simmered Kailan
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Kailan is quite often known as the princess vegetable due to the intense care a farmer has to shower on it to make sure it grows well (it's a dinner time fav of many caterpillars and bugs). Thankfully cooking it is pretty straightforward as long as you have the right sauce, accompaniments. 
PS: Red-dates, goji-berries, rice wine, and lean meat make this a confinement friendly dish for mothers looking for a change in their daily meals

name: Winter Melon Meatball Soup (Serves 2)
allergy: Contains gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
Created by Prepped in conjunction with Knorr.
We got a bit FOMO when we were working on bringing the Knorr campaign to life, so here's our take on a Knorr Savorich inspired recipe. We love the use of wintermelon in soups as it adds a refreshing snap to a rich soup without overpowering the flavorful broth, throw in some meatballs and cellophane noodles and you have a soup to warm you up if you get caught in an afternoon thunderstorm.

name: Wongbok and Garlic Shoots
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description:
A dish inspired by our early cooking days when we didn't have the time to cook that often. To combat the lack of frequency, we bought vegetables that kept well in the fridge, yet are versatile and easily compatible with others so that a quick stir-fry is never too far away.
Every element has its own unique level of sweetness and crunch that allows it to stand out from the overall dish when eaten, but also builds a foundation for the next vegetable on your next bite. Layer of taste anyone?

name: Xinjiang Cumin Beef
allergy: Contains crustaceans, fish, soy, gluten. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Hailing from the nomadic Xinjiang region, this dish, bursting with bold flavors from the generous use of spices and herbs, will transport you directly to the steppes of central asia. Traditionally made with lamb, we chose to avoid the gamey-ness by utilizing tender slices of beef flank instead. Toss in a handful of king oyster mushrooms to fully absorb all the flavors and juices and you'll never want to have it any other way.

name: Yau Mak with Mustard Greens
allergy: Contains gluten, crustaceans, fish. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: We've recently been infatuated with this seemingly plebian vegetable: Yau Mak Chye. While it looks like the more popular romaine lettuce (some even name it baby romaine), the lack of a bitter note makes it, in our opinion, superior to cook with. Flash stir-fry it over high heat and you'll have yourself a vegetable with the crunch of a raw salad but also the developed sweet notes from a vegetable that has been cooked to perfection.

name: Yuxiang King Oyster Mushrooms
allergy: Contains gluten, soy. May contain traces of tree nuts
description: Yuxiang is a sauce that routinely confuses us. It literally translates to fish fragrance.... except the sauce neither contains fish nor is fish particularly fragrant. What we are not confused by is that the sauce tastes amazing. We've decided to make king oyster mushrooms the star of this show, showcasing its ability to soak up all that sauce making every bite an explosion of taste and flavors.

name: “Claypot” chicken and tofu
allergy: Contains traces of gluten and tree nuts
description:
You may not have a claypot at home but that shouldn't stop you from making this amazing dish. Seared chicken and tofu medallions tossed in a medley or crispy snap peas, bamboo shoots and carrots and coated in a fragrant rich umami sauce. Is it better in a claypot? Everything is better in a claypot!! That said, this version comes pretty darn close. 
PS: Make sure to prep an extra serving of rice for this delicious treat, that carb-free diet of yours can wait another day.

name: Balinese Roasted Chicken
description:
Fragrant spices, a sweet savory glaze, refreshing limes, now that's what we call a rockstar marinade. Keeping with our tradition of a summer Christmas, this year, we venture to the vacation island of Bali where this grilled chicken reigns supreme. Pair this with a refreshingly floral sambal matah and you have a main great for both potlucks or a small christmas gathering by the pool.
Chicken weighs around 1.5kg - 1.7kg, and it feeds 3-4.

name: Braised Stuffed Eggplants
description:
Stuffing is a must for Christmas, but this year we wanted to move away from all that carb loading and upgrade our stuffing game with something meatier. So we’ve decided to stuff the meatiest tasting vegetable we know--the eggplant--with the meatiest stuffing we can dream of--a pine nut, mushroom Moroccan-inspired beef filling. Braise it with a little assam spice brew and you’ll get a dish that you’ll probably reach for before the actual mains.
Feeds 4 pax

name: Buddha's Delight
description:
We all know about the Buddha's temptation (佛跳牆) a dish so legendarily decadent it can tempt vegetarian monk to cross the picket fence into a carnivore's world. But let's not do something so mischievous at the start of the new year.
Instead, how about the buddha's delight a dish so delightful one forgets about the need to have meat? Made with 9 different vegetables, this medley of taste, textures and color will whet the appetite of even the staunchest carnivore. 
Serving size: Feeds 4-6 people

name: Buttermilk pancakes with burnt apples and gula melaka butter (Serves 2)
description: REAL BUTTERMILK PANCAKES!!!! If you know how hard it is to find buttermilk in Singapore, you'd appreciate the fact that we not only have buttermilk, but we have pretty darned good fresh buttermilk made locally! The acidity in the buttermilk helps to activate the baking soda while also imparting a slight tang, giving you a truly complex tasting stack of fluffy pancakes (move over, premixed store-bought versions). Top that with our freshly made from scratch burnt apple sauce, and a dollop of gula melaka butter, and you might end up not want to share this serving for 2 with anyone.

name: Calabrese Hasselbacked Potatoes
description:
We love a good bomba calabrese sauce.....but as the name sounds, man is it spicy. To make this a lot more Christmas friendly, we went to work making our own. The result? A milder calabrese sauce packed with more sweetness and floral notes than usual. Sure, it isn't your traditional bomba calabrese, but load that sauce on top of some hasselbacked potatoes and you'll never roast another potato the same way again.
PS: Why go through the trouble of hasselbacking a potato? Well, because those ridges open up so beautifully when roasted, capturing all that calabrese sauce in its crevices (kinda like a well paired pasta shape).

name: Canton Style Cod
description:
No CNY dinner is complete without a fish. Gently steamed snow cod, bathed in a ginger scallion infused soy dressing and topped with all the herb fixins synonymous with a Cantonese style fish. Simply classic, while also delectably tasty.
Traditions typically call for a whole steamed fish, but we often struggle to find a big enough steamer, or enough money in the bank to splurge on a whole snow cod. Our hack....fish steaks: thick enough to keep its shape when steaming, yet dainty enough to eat with a pair of chopsticks.
PS: Did you know snow cod in this region is not actually a cod, it is actually the more prized Chilean Seabass, or as we like to call it the Patagonian Toothfish. Ugly name, amazing fish.
Serving size: Feeds 2-3 people

quantity.raw: Light Soy Sauce, Olive Oil, Sesame Oil,  Sugar

name: Dirty Nasi Kuning
description:
Rice is good, but rice spiked with flavor is great, so groundbreaking we could eat it as a dish on its own. Chicken rice, Nasi Lemak, Biryani...the list goes on. Among them is the underrated Nasi Kuning, turmeric rice. So what could make it better? Making it dirty of course.
Using our favorite cajun technique, we added in northern-thai styled chicken sausage, bell pepper, onions to create a base packed with flavor, then cooked the turmeric rice using its traditional lemak method. The result: a side so delicious we started squirreling away portion to keep for the days after. Sharing is caring, unless it is dirty nasi kuning.

name: Dong Po Pork
description:
Whole pork belly, braised with top-shelf Shaoxing wine, 2 kinds of soy sauce and yellow rock sugar. Shaoxing helps to cut the fattiness of the pork belly, while the slow caramelization of the rock sugar allows the soy to penetrate the meat before thickening it into the eventual sauce. Equal parts fat and lean meat, this melt in your mouth dish will have you going back for seconds.
PS: Our longest cooking time kit to date....but trust us, it is going to be worth it. Thankfully most of the time is spent letting the dish simmer in its own sauce and juices worth it. Thankfully most of the time is spent letting the dish simmer in its own sauce and juices.
Serving size: Feeds 3-4 people

quantity.raw: Shaoxing Wine, Light Soy Sauce, Dark Soy Sauce, Rock Sugar

name: Drunken Chicken
description:
We love a good porchetta or lechon: stuffing all those herbs and aromatics into the center of the meat imparts a great flavor during roasting, but also adds a bit of texture with each bite. So, what if we did the same with an otherwise very traditional poached chicken? Our rendition of an herbal drunken chicken of course
First, we roll our chicken thighs around a bundle of spring onions, ginger and wolfberries. The gentle steaming process helps to release those flavors while keeping the chicken moist. Drizzle on a herbal sauce made from dangui, red dates and the chicken drippings from the steaming process and say hi to what is possible your new favorite side dish.
Serving size: Feeds 2-3 people

quantity.raw: Water, Shaoxing, Rock Sugar, Sea Salt

name: Elotes (Mexican Street Corn)
description:
Nothing beats chargrilled street corn loaded with peppers, onions and topped with cotija. To make it a tad more christmas party friendly, we've opted to de-cob the corn to reduce the risk of getting all that juicy goodness over your christmas outfit. 
Feeds 3-4 pax (as a side dish with a main).

name: Hot Honey Pan-roasted Padrons and Halloumi
description:
Charred padrons and halloumi are always a crowd pleaser, and the mild pops of sweet, smokey, bitter and salty flavours make the dish the perfect appetizer. To make it truly memorable, we've paired this dish with a mildly fermented hot honey infused with shallots, garlic and thyme to add some extra pizzazz and to truly kickstart the season’s festivities.Warning: This honey is so good, you may end up drizzling it on everything. 
Feeds 3 - 4 pax

name: Lily Bud Stewed Chicken
description:
Note: Large serving size. Meal feeds 3-4 people. Rice not included.
Some of our earliest memories as kids were that of getting all the cousins around around the dinner table prepping for the night's CNY reunion dinner. One of the chores: tying lily bulb knots! This chore was best done by the deft nimble hands of children, or so they told us (we're starting to realize how gullible we were).
While the buds get used in a variety of dishes, none were more memorable than the humble stewed chicken. Lovingly simmered with mushrooms, scallions, ginger and lily buds, this dish sent aromas wafting through the kitchen and was eaten both the night of and the day after.
PS: we've added chestnuts (a thing we learnt to love in stews during our time in Korea) for an added touch of warmth and  sweetness. Just remember to keep them covered under the liquid while simmering so that they fully soften.

quantity.raw: Oyster Sauce, Water, Sugar, Sesame Oil

name: Mala butter mushroom aglio olio (Serves 2)
description:
Yes....aglio olio traditionally uses crushed red chilli flakes, but (bear with us here) why settle for just one flavor when you can have the duality of both spice and tingly-ness? Two is better than one, so you'll can also look forward to a tingly mala taste from the addition of the creamy Mala Butter! Toss in 5 different types of mushrooms to soak up all that goodness and your guest won't believe you whipped this dish up in just 10 minutes.
PS: If you're worried about spice, fret not, the creaminess and tang from the freshly churned cultured butter helps to mediate the fiery notes of the mala, making this a gentle introduction to the world of mala
PPS: those wanting a more fiery kick: we added an optional pack of crushed red chilli flakes if you really want to dial up the heat

name: Maple Cider Glazed Baby-back Ribs
description:
You've heard of a reverse seared steak, but how about a reverse seared slab of dry rubbed ribs? Same technique, same amazing tender fall-off-the-bone results! Adding an apple cider maple glaze right before searing creates scrumptious caramelized bits, while a green herb chimichurri helps balance out the flavors for ribs you'll be craving well into the new year.
Feeds 3-4 pax

name: Maple Glazed Butternut Squash
description:
The most popular side from our first 2 christmas menu! We've brought it back in all its glory!
What people loved about it:

Hasselbacking the squash made it "fall off the bone"
The glaze is to die for
The christmas spice rub made my house smell like christmas for the whole day!

quantity.raw: Butter, Maple syrup, Honey, Brown sugar, Cinnamon, Nutmeg

name: Maple Harissa Roasted Pumpkin
description:
This is for you….yes you….the one that’s going to be doing all the cooking. If you’re like us, you’ll most likely be spending the day after recuperating from all the hard work of hosting/cooking and all you’ll want is some couch time and a quick but delicious lunch. Well, this is the dish: prep more of this during the big meal and hope for leftovers (or do what we do, and squirrel some away for the day after). What’s not to like? Sweetness from the pumpkin, creaminess from the tahini maple dressing, and a slight smokey kick from the harissa; this side served hot goes great with a roasted chicken or some ribs.
Better yet, save it till the next day, mash it up and slather it on some toast or in a wrap and you’ll have what is probably the best holiday hangover brunch dish we can think of.
Feeds 3-4 pax

name: Miso Gindara Cod
description:
Gindara is a bit of an unheralded fish, more of a if you know you KNOW kind of fish. Sometimes called the black cod, this is, in our opinion, the best fish on earth. Sure, the snow cod is silkier and more buttery, but you try eating more than a few mouthfuls of that fish without thinking of the word jelak. Yes Atlantic cod and haddock flake amazingly well, but where's that wagyu like intramuscular fat?
This is where the Gindara comes in, right in the perfect intersection of decadently flakey yet still lean enough that you'd fight for seconds. Cure it with a rich miso base then served with some yakitori negi skewers and people might just forget about the ang pow you still owe them from last year.

Light Soy Sauce, Mirin, Sugar, Sake

name: Miso snow cod with kabocha sweet potato mash (Serves 2)
description:
Once in a while, we come across an ingredient so unique and eye-opening that it calls for an equally stunning recipe. That's the challenge we received when we tried the Yuzu Butter from Atas Butter. To highlight the explosion of flora notes and citrus tangs of the yuzu butter, we co-opted a miso black cod recipe, dialed the luxe factor up to 100 by using snow cod, and paired it with a slow roasted kabocha sweet potato mash. Let that yuzu butter melt all over the rich silky cod and into the mash, and get ready for what can only be describe as dining bliss.
P.S. Prefer a more full bodied umami taste? Opt for the kombu butter! It's complex and savory, and you'd might even think you're sitting by the ocean.

name: Mum's Style Chicken Cabbage Braise (Serves 2)
description:
Growing up, this dish was a staple whenever mum had a busy schedule and had little time to cook dinner. We would come back to a one pot braise with lots of chicken, cabbage and mushrooms sitting on the stove, ready whenever we wanted dinner. 
Years later, long after we'd moved out, we'd sometimes find ourselves craving this simple, home-style dish that could be found in no restaurant or food stall anywhere. Perhaps it was deemed too simple and unfancy, but we love it for its wholesome flavours, and the fact that re-heating it only makes the ingredients meld even better together.
Over the years, we’ve tried to re-create it on our own, and we’ve found that it’s impossible to achieve the same taste when cooked in a portion for one. Turns out it needs bulk to work its magic, which also means it was never meant to be eaten alone.
So find someone to share it with. Or don't. We fully endorse finishing the whole pot solo, no judgment here.
A little tip: you can even cook this in a rice cooker.

name: Pan Roasted Lemon Asparagus Medley
description: A tangy burst of sunshine, this side will help cut through all those heavy decadent flavor profiles of a traditional holiday feast. Preserved lemons add a ton of bright yet savory flavor notes while the sharp twang of the red radishes helps to further cut through the grease. Mix that all in with crunchy spears of asparagus and baby corn and this palette cleanser will better allow you to enjoy all the other sides, while also fend off the dreaded post meal food coma (hopefully).

name: Peruvian Roasted Chicken
description: Marinated with 2 types of hard-to-find-in-these-parts chili pastes (Aji amarillo and Aji panca)for more depth of flavour, a dash of lime citrus soy, and a rub of cumin, pepper and salt, this roasted spatchcock chicken will make you question why you even put up with the muted flavors of dry chirstmas turkey for so many years. Pair that with a fresh tangy cilantro chili mayo made in-house, and that's what you call finger licking good.

name: Pistachio Crusted Burnt Apple Pork Roll
description:
Yes, apples go great with pork, but you know what's better? When we slow caramelize apples under gentle heat and let all those natural sugars deepen in flavor to create a house-made apple sauce. Now slather that applesauce all over your pork roll, stuff it full with herbs and mozzarella and encase it all in a parmesan pistachio crust...Now that's a show stopper.
The roll feeds 3 people, if eaten as a main.

name: Smoked butter air-fried chicken and pancakes (Serves 2)
description: REAL BUTTERMILK !!!! That means two things....PANCAKES and FRIED CHICKEN. You may already know buttermilk is great for making fluffy pancakes, but did you know that marinating a slab of chicken overnight in buttermilk with a heap full of spices will result in what can only be described as borderline magic? The result: a perfectly tender piece of chicken with a flaky crust, ready to go on top of your pancakes. Now top that off with some fresh, locally churned smoked butter from Atas Butter, a drizzle of maple syrup, and pancakes can now be considered a responsible adult meal.

name: Smoked haddock and salmon two fish roast
description: You've probably heard of the turducken (chicken in a duck in a turkey), say hi to it's fish cousin. Two slabs of marbled Atlantic salmon stuffed with smoked Norwegian haddock, coriander garlic compound butter, and lemon. The smoked haddock imparts a smokey hue to the salmon while the compound butter bastes the salmon from the inside out as it roasts. Top this all off with our home made roasted pepper chickpea sauce and this year's Christmas showstopper will be yours.

name: Sundried Tomato Butter Basted Chicken
description:
Roasting a bird can sometimes be daunting, especially if you want to get perfectly cooked thighs without drying out the breast. Here's our little secret: - Step 1: Spatchcock the chicken so it cooks evenly throughout - Step 2: Vacuum marinade the chicken to ensure maximum taste absorption - Step 3: Massage our amazing sundried tomato and basil butter under the skin of the chicken allowing the breast meat to confit as you roast it - Step 4: More of that yummy tomato butter to smother the chicken to get a juicy yet crispy chicken
Fret not...we've done all that for you, so all you need to do now is to pop it into an oven and get ready to smother all that juicy meat with a basil lime mayo and tuck in!
Feeds 3-4, if eaten as a main.

name: Tahini maple root vegetable roast
description: Roasted pumpkin, beets, zucchini, chickpeas and onions all smothered in a delectable tahini maple dressing. Slow roasting allows for all the natural sugars in the root vegetables to develop, enhancing the unique natural flavors of the root vegetables: (sweetness from the pumpkin, flora from the zucchini, earthy from the beets, savory from the onions, and nutty from the chickpeas). Oils from the tahini based dressing create great flavor transporters ensuring each mouthful is packed full of flavors sure to tickle your taste buds.

name: Truffle Treasures
description:
Crunch is the often forgotten texture, with this dish we celebrate the different types of crunch from our favorite vegetables. Cook this following the recommend timing, and you'll have a complexly layered dish full of snaps, clicks, pops and crackles all smothered in a decadent truffle laced sauce.
Note: This dish is portioned as a shareable dish for 3-5 pax.

quantity.raw: Vegetarian stock, Sugar, Salt, Water, Truffle oil

name: Urab Sayur
description:
Freshly grate a coconut then toast with aromatic shallots, lemongrass, kefir lime leaves and a hint of chilli. Top this over a bed of crunchy long beans, tender bean sprouts and leafy spinach and you have yourself a vegan taste bomb that can be both served hot or as a cold side.
Sounds daunting? Thankfully you have us to do all that prep :-)
